title: KV layer ghost-entry playbook
content:
Purpose:
Short hands-on scratchpad for reproducing and triaging intermittent 'ghost' KV entries that appear when sequence length crosses boundary conditions (1024/2048), and to correlate with attention kernel selection behaviour. Intended for quick experiments and breadcrumbs to convert into a proper incident write-up once we have a root cause.

Observed symptoms (high level):
- Sporadic stale/incorrect KV hits during long-context requests (mostly sequences >= 1024 + multiple prefix segments).
- GPU-side attention kernel sometimes chosen as 'attn_fallback' even when 'fused_attn_v2' should be compatible for the given rotary/seq dims. Suspect mismatch between server-side kernel capability map and runtime decision.
- When ghost entries occur, generated tokens occasionally repeat a few steps or reintroduce earlier tokens (small loops) — suggests KV read returned a wrong/value-shifted vector for particular key indices.

Repro environment (quick):
- image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runtime:dev-2024-10-30
- model: redwood-alpha-3b-rlif (rotary dims 64, kv-block-size 128)
- hw: p4d.24xlarge / 8x A100-stubs in local repro (single GPU test also fails reproducibly for the sequence case)

Minimal reproduce (local):
1) build a test file of repeated alternating prompts so kv offsets line up with wrap boundary (see tests/fixtures/kv-border-seqs.txt attached to this note).
2) run binary with kv tracing flags:
   export DEBUG_KV=1 DEBUG_ATTN=1
   ./bin/run_infer --model redwood-alpha-3b-rlif --input tests/fixtures/kv-border-seqs.txt --max-tokens 512 --seqlen 2048 --trace-kv /tmp/kvtrace.log
3) grep for suspicious offsets:
   grep "KV: found" /tmp/kvtrace.log | sed -n '1,200p'

Example commands already tried (and outcomes):
- toggled KV wrap mode:
  --kv-wrap=modulo -> reproduces ghost hits in ~40% runs
  --kv-wrap=clamp  -> reduces incidence (~5%) but not eliminated (suggests wrap mode influences frequency but not root cause)

- forced single-threaded CPU kernel to isolate race:
  OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 ./bin/run_infer ... -> ghost entry still appears (so not purely OMP race on CPU path)

- forced unified fused attention kernel:
  RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=fused_attn_v2 ./bin/run_infer ... -> if fused kernel used consistently, ghost hits drop to ~1/40 runs (non-zero)

- toggled continuous-batching off/on (server config):
  continuous_batching=false -> incidence increases (likely because batching aggregates offsets differently)

Relevant log snippets (copied raw):
[2024-11-05 14:21:08.623] WARN KVCache: found ghost entry at global_offset=2047 local_idx=1023 token_id=4285 ttl=0 owner_thread=12
[2024-11-05 14:21:08.624] DEBUG AttnRouter: chosen_kernel=fallback_v1 model_caps=(fused_attn_v2:false, attn_v1:true) runtime_caps=(fused_attn_v2:true)
[2024-11-05 14:21:08.625] ERROR KVRead: expected key_hash=0x7f3a12, got=0x2b9d03 ; indices used: head=7 slot=1023 computed_rel_offset=-1

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Offset computation edge-case: when absolute_seq % kv_block_size == 0 we compute relative offsets that momentarily become negative (signed underflow in an int32 cast) and then used as unsigned index into the GPU KV buffer, grabbing the wrong slot. Evidence: computed_rel_offset=-1 in log above.
2) Kernel selection mismatch: we have a stale capability table on the request path where the router prefers attn_v1 fallback even though fused_attn_v2 is OK: fused kernel handles boundary indexing differently (wrap-safe). When fallback chosen, fallback path has slightly different offset arithmetic and exposes the bug.
3) Incomplete KV invalidation for canary rollouts: when a model variant is rolled out with different kv-block-size or rotary dims, existing in-memory KVs are not fully invalidated for pinned customers. Leads to ghost reads if runtime doesn't clear per-model metadata.
4) Memory aliasing/race in GPU eviction path: concurrent eviction + read where a freed slot is immediately reused; timing difference amplified at scale.

Micro-experiments and quick numbers (notes):
- Run A: kv_wrap=modulo, router default -> 41 runs -> 16 failures (~39%).
- Run B: kv_wrap=clamp, force fused_attn_v2 -> 40 runs -> 1 failure (~2.5%).
- Run C: kv_wrap=clamp, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, force fused -> 40 runs -> 1 failure (same as B).
- Run D: same as B but with --disable-prefetch -> failures up to 6/40 (~15%) -> suggests prefetch path influences timing.

Immediate mitigations to try (short term):
- Add assert in offset computation to check for negative offsets and early fail (safer than silent wrong read).
- Force fused_attn_v2 for all deployments where model rotary/seq dims permit (fast patch) — reduces incidents significantly in experiments.
- Add a small per-request KV validity token (incrementing generation id) read-checked on GPU read to avoid using stale slot values.
- Add a canary that exercises boundary seqlen values during rollout smoke tests.

Longer term / root-cause work items: (convert to tickets)
- INF-2247: audit all places that compute relative_offset: enforce 64-bit arithmetic and unit tests for boundary values for block sizes 1..1024.
- INF-2248: add kernel capability propagation test between decision/routing layer and worker; include a deterministic override harness in CI.
- INF-2250: investigate eviction path race window (profiler traces + synthetic timers) — instrument slot lifecycle timestamps.

Debug breadcrumbs / artifacts I left behind:
- /tmp/kvtrace.log.* copies (full runs) on my laptop (Aisha) and small clips uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-debug/kv/kv-ghost-2024-11-05.tar.gz
- local repro fixture: tests/fixtures/kv-border-seqs.txt (contains templated inputs that align tokens to block boundaries)
- small python script used to scan traces and produce the micro-experiment table: tools/kv/scan_kv_traces.py (line 1..200 contains quick parsing heuristics)

Next steps (this week):
- (Today) push quick assert around relative_offset compute to dev branch and run full CI including unit tests for 1..2048 seq values. (PR -> runtime/patches/kv-offset-assert)
- (Tomorrow) run extended repro on internal perf cluster 8x A100, with prefetch toggles to replicate D. Collect kernel selection logs.
- (Fri) meet with Applied ML (Priya) and Platform (Miguel) to discuss rollout mitigation (force fused kernel) and draft incident postmortem template.

Open questions / things to confirm:
- Are there any model variants that legitimately use different kv_block_size for same model name across rollouts? (I think earlier redwood-alpha-3b-rlif experiment had a variant with 256 block size during a canary).
- Do we maintain a per-worker capability table that can be desynced from the router? How and when is it refreshed?

Quick notes to self (actionable):
- grep for "computed_rel_offset=-1" across s3 traces to quantify how many unique runs triggered underflow.
- Add unit test: for offsets in [0, kv_block_size*8] compute mapping for both clamp and modulo modes.
- Make a small repro that toggles only the kernel selection (simulated) to verify the math difference between fallback and fused kernels.

If you pick this up: start by running the micro-experiments listed above and upload the kvtrace logs to the Jira ticket INF-2247. If you need direct context ping me (Aisha) or Miguel in #serving-runtime.

-- Aisha
